title: Top Scorer on S. Korean Exam Admits to AI Cheating
paragraphs: To become a licensed tax accountant in South Korea, candidates must pass a national exam.
Although it's known to be very difficult, this year's top scorer got almost every question right on one part of the exam.
However, the candidate has now confessed that he used AI to cheat.

The exam was done in two parts, with the first part done in April, and the second in July. The candidate — who is being referred to only by his surname, Han — got a score of 397.5 out of 400 on the first part, and 663 out of 800 on the second part.
That means he got only one out of 160 questions wrong on the first part of the exam.
Many were suspicious of this score, and some said he must have cheated using smart glasses. At first, Han denied this.
However, on November 15, he admitted that he had used a small camera to take photos of the exam questions. He then sent the photos to an AI tool and checked the answers on his smartphone.
The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said it had received a written confession from Han through his lawyer.
In a video, Han said he cheated because he wanted to make money, and he wanted to make his parents proud by becoming a tax accountant.
The case has raised concerns about how easily people can cheat on important exams.
Candidates are told to turn off their phones and put them in their bags, but exam supervisors do not collect them.
Han has given the police his camera, laptop and smartphone, and said he will "fully cooperate with the police to identify and prevent cheating in future examinations."

The Human Resources Development Service of Korea — which is in charge of the exam — has also apologized for failing to notice the cheating. It said it would take legal action against Han, and work to make future exams more secure.
